newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH TRAVEL AGENCY ORBIS TO BE PRIVATISED IN Q4.
newsitem.headline: POLISH TRAVEL AGENCY ORBIS TO BE PRIVATISED IN Q4.

text.p: Polish travel agency Orbis SA will be privatised in the fourth quarter of 1997 through the sale of state-treasury shares and an issue of 8.5 million new shares, the company's deputy president said on Friday.

"According to our plans the sale of series A and a series B issue will take place in the fourth quarter....After the additional issue the number of shares will increase by 8,523,625 shares," Ireneusz Weglowski told Reuters.
Weglowski said the sale of each series would be carried out simultaneously.
Weglowski said that after the sales the State Treasury would have a minority share in the firm but gave no details.

Earlier this year the company said 15 percent of its shares would go to employees, 10 percent to pension funds created in the reform of the social security system, and five percent would be retained by the treasury.
Weglowski said Orbis did not seek a strategic investory and no such negotiations were taking place.
He said funds from the privatisation would go toward modernising the firm's 54 hotels and buying new ones, a goal the company has estimated needs 450 million zlotys.
Orbis, employing around 10,000 people, made a net profit of 28 million zlotys in 1996 and about 19 million in 1995.
